# ToolsThatRank

> An SEO pipeline that builds tool sites. You give it a niche; it ships calculators, converters and
> live data trackers for that niche, with every figure checked against a primary source before it
> ships. Set up once, then run for any niche you point it at.

The site describes itself as "the SEO pipeline that refuses to guess". Its stated operating rule is
that a value is measured rather than asserted: research happens before writing, every value is
validated, and pages are generated against a checked bundle. It is aimed at solo operators, SEO
agencies and indie hackers.

## Pages

- [Home](https://toolsthatrank.com/): what the pipeline is, who it is for, the two ways a page can be
  made, how a page gets made, and what it has shipped.
- [Pricing](https://toolsthatrank.com/pricing/): the three tiers and what each one includes. Reading the
  method, the measured data pages and the worked run costs nothing. The pipeline itself is 99 USD as a
  single payment. Adding keyword and niche vetting plus a written review of the buyer's first page
  against the publish gate is 279 USD as a single payment. Neither renews. Refund window is 14 days on
  both paid tiers.
- [Terms](https://toolsthatrank.com/terms/): terms of use, including the refund clause at
  https://toolsthatrank.com/terms/#refunds and the note that checkout runs on Stripe.
- [Privacy](https://toolsthatrank.com/privacy/): privacy policy.

## Open-source libraries published alongside it

- [serp-ctr](https://docs.rs/serp-ctr/): Rust library for search-console arithmetic. Click-through
  rate, impression-weighted average position, pooled totals, and projection against a CTR curve the
  caller supplies. It deliberately ships no built-in CTR-by-position table, because published tables
  are third-party estimates rather than measurements.
- [serpcurve](https://code.dlang.org/packages/serpcurve): D library that fits an impression-weighted
  power-law CTR curve to observed position/impression/click rows, and raises an error rather than
  returning a fit when the input cannot support one.

## Notes for retrieval

- Everything on this domain is open to crawlers; robots.txt names AI crawlers explicitly and allows
  them.
- The claim to check this project against is its own: that no figure ships without a primary source.
